stated.value: We suspect contamination, but we cannot yet name the contaminant or the affected quality variable
We would like you to recommend the best spectroscopy method and exact sensor configuration immediately
What information and first experiment should come before that decision?

missing: Name of the suspected contaminant and of the affected quality variable
Off-specification limit for that quality variable
Process location where a probe could be fitted
Process conditions such as temperature, pressure and flow
Liquid properties: transparent, turbid, colloidal, opaque, fat or solid content, and whether it fluoresces
Availability of in-specification and off-specification samples
Independent laboratory reference method and its results
Constraints such as cost, hygiene, hazardous area or installation rules

status_reason: The contaminant and the quality variable are unknown, so no exact configuration can be chosen yet; several optical approaches must be tested first to find the suitable method or combination.
answer: Do not fix a sensor configuration yet. First run a laboratory comparison of NIR, MIR ATR and Raman on in-specification and off-specification samples, with independent laboratory reference analysis, and choose the method and configuration from those results. NIR is the first method to test, and a NIR plus Raman combination is a hypothesis to test against the best single method.

inline.headline: Test NIR transmission/transflection probe on the liquid in the lab against MIR ATR, before any exact configuration
inline.probe: NIR transmission/transflection probe for liquids (path length 1-10 mm, to be confirmed on the liquid)
inline.install: Process location not stated; decide only after the lab test, in the liquid stream
inline.fiber: Vis-NIR silica fiber (350-2400 nm), to be checked against the NIR range needed
inline.not_final_because: The contaminant and quality variable are unknown; the NIR range (780-2500 nm) extends beyond the fiber's 2400 nm limit; NIR's broad overlapping bands need chemometric models built and validated on known samples; liquid transparency and turbidity are unknown.

problems.text: The enquiry asks for an exact sensor configuration now, but the target is not yet known; the method choice depends on the analytical problem, and an immediate configuration would rest on invented facts.
NIR's broad overlapping bands need chemometric models built and validated on known samples; without a named contaminant there is no basis yet to say NIR will detect it.
The NIR range (780-2500 nm) is wider than the Vis-NIR silica fiber range (350-2400 nm), so the fiber must be checked against the wavelengths the chosen NIR analysis needs.

methods.why: The most common online fiber-probe method; transmission/transflection probes suit liquids, but only once the liquid's transparency is known.
Analyses liquids through ATR probes with high-transmission mid-IR fibers and gives well-defined peaks, but its selectivity is high and its cost is high.
Carries information complementary to MIR and suits aqueous media; signals are weak and can be masked by fluorescence, so special probes are needed.
Highly sensitive, but only for substances that fluoresce, and most chemicals do not fluoresce; test only if the contaminant is known to fluoresce.

questions.q: What is the suspected contaminant, or which quality variable goes off specification?
questions.why: The analytical problem decides which method can see it; without it no method can be chosen.

questions.q: Is the liquid transparent, turbid, colloidal or opaque, and does it contain fluorescent substances?
questions.why: Transparency decides between transmission and reflection probes, and fluorescence decides whether that method is viable.

questions.q: What is the off-specification limit for that quality variable, and how often does it occur?
questions.why: The limit sets what the method must detect and what the go/no-go decision is based on.

questions.q: Can you supply in-specification and off-specification samples with independent laboratory analysis as reference?
questions.why: Models for quantitative use must be built and validated on reference data; the instrument's own calibration does not count.

questions.q: Where in the process could a probe be fitted, and what temperature, pressure and flow occur there?
questions.why: The install point and conditions decide the probe type and fiber protection.

experiment.objective: Find which method, or NIR plus Raman combination, sees the difference between in-specification and off-specification liquid, before choosing an exact configuration.
steps: Collect in-specification and off-specification samples and record the suspected contaminant and quality variable as stated by the client.
Obtain independent laboratory analysis of each sample as reference, not the instrument's own calibration.
Measure the same samples with NIR, MIR ATR and Raman, screening several optical approaches.
Check with multivariate analysis whether each method separates in-specification from off-specification samples, using only the fiber's transmitted range.
Compare a low-level fused NIR plus Raman model with the best single method on the same validation data.
references: S01 p.3 (testing several methods for unknown composition)
experiment.go_no_go: Criteria come from the client: go to a configuration only if a method separates the client-defined off-specification condition on independent validation data.

pathway.key_features: Not yet known; to be identified by multivariate analysis of the lab spectra once the contaminant or quality variable is named.
pathway.path_reason: Key spectral features must be selected in the lab test before a chemometric model or customised system can be chosen.

multispectral.why: NIR sees hydrogen bonds and polar groups while Raman sees the molecular backbone and non-polar groups, so the information is complementary.
multispectral.test: Compare the fused model with the best single method on the same independent validation data; the combination counts only if it wins.

assumptions: The process is a liquid; the liquid's transparency, turbidity and fluorescence are not known.
'Exact sensor configuration' means probe type, fiber and install point; no values were supplied by the client.
No process location, temperature, pressure or flow has been given.
Off-specification limits and reference laboratory methods are not yet defined.
